How someone could cause the problem: Steal a staff password or session and impersonate a reviewer.
Potential impact: C/I: Read private cases, approve misleading replies or change tasks. Learners receive instructions from someone posing as staff.
Evidence to check: Sign-in records, MFA events, session activity and actions performed by the affected account.
Proposed safeguard: Individual staff accounts, phishing-resistant MFA, protected sessions and prompt session revocation.
How to spot the problem: Alert on unusual sign-ins, suspicious session reuse and unexpected reviewer activity.
Proposed owner and escalation trigger: Identity administrator. Escalate suspected staff-account takeover immediately to security.
Residual risk: A stolen active session or compromised staff device may bypass login protections.

How someone could cause the problem: Compromise an editor account and publish altered dates, fees or requirements through a weak approval process.
Potential impact: I/mission: Learners receive incorrect guidance and may miss deadlines or make unsuitable choices.
Evidence to check: Document version history, editor identity, publication approvals and the exact source version used for a reply.
Proposed safeguard: Restrict editing; require separate publication approval; retain versions; give the API read-only access.
How to spot the problem: Alert on publication changes and compare sampled replies against approved source versions.
Proposed owner and escalation trigger: Program content owner. Escalate any unauthorised publication or harmful guidance already issued.
Residual risk: Authorised editors or approvers can still make mistakes or have their accounts compromised.

STRIDE type and service part: Repudiation: staff console and logging service
How someone could cause the problem: Use a shared account or alter audit records, then deny approving a reply or closing a task.
Potential impact: I/mission: The academy cannot reliably investigate disputed decisions or identify unresolved cases.
Evidence to check: Approval records, task history, actor IDs, timestamps, audit gaps and log-deletion permissions.
Proposed safeguard: Use unique identities and protected, append-only audit records. Link approvals to the exact reply or task version.
How to spot the problem: Monitor missing audit events, collection failures, deletion attempts and actions without approval records.
Proposed owner and escalation trigger: Operations lead. Escalate suspected audit tampering immediately; investigate gaps affecting approvals urgently.
Residual risk: Logs support attribution but cannot prove intent. Actions using a stolen account can appear legitimate.

STRIDE type and service part: Information disclosure: web client and API
How someone could cause the problem: Change a case identifier in a request where the API fails to check ownership or assignment.
Potential impact: C: Another learner’s questions, identity or support history become visible.
Evidence to check: Access-control tests using fictional cases, case-access events and API permission rules.
Proposed safeguard: Enforce case-level permissions on every API request and return only necessary fields.
How to spot the problem: Monitor unexpected cross-case access and repeated access denials; run access-control regression checks.
Proposed owner and escalation trigger: API lead. Escalate any confirmed unauthorised read to security and the privacy lead immediately.
Residual risk: Authorised staff may misuse legitimate access; a new endpoint could introduce a permission defect.

STRIDE type and service part: Denial of service: web client, API, AI provider integration, logging service and staff queues
How someone could cause the problem: Submit large volumes of requests or oversized questions to exhaust processing, AI budgets, storage or staff capacity.
Potential impact: A/mission: Learners cannot obtain help; staff face backlogs and additional costs.
Evidence to check: Request volumes, payload sizes, response times, error rates, queue depth, AI usage and storage growth.
Proposed safeguard: Apply request, size and AI-usage limits, bounded queues, timeouts and spending caps. Provide a manual support route.
How to spot the problem: Alert on traffic spikes, queue growth, slow responses, failures and unusual spending.
Proposed owner and escalation trigger: Operations lead. Escalate when legitimate support is blocked or approved capacity/budget limits are reached.
Residual risk: Distributed attacks, provider outages and genuine demand spikes can still reduce service.

STRIDE type and service part: Elevation of privilege: API and staff console
How someone could cause the problem: Modify a client-supplied role or directly call a staff endpoint where permission checks are missing.
Potential impact: C/I: Access restricted cases, approve replies or change task assignments without authority.
Evidence to check: Tests of staff endpoints with learner identities, role configuration, privilege-change records and service-account permissions.
Proposed safeguard: Derive roles from trusted identity information; deny access by default; check staff permissions server-side; minimise service privileges.
How to spot the problem: Alert on unexpected role grants and learner identities attempting staff operations.
Proposed owner and escalation trigger: API lead. Escalate any successful unauthorised staff action or unexpected privilege grant immediately.
Residual risk: Incorrect role assignments and compromised privileged accounts remain possible.

STRIDE type and service part: Tampering; possible information disclosure: knowledge source, API and AI provider
How someone could cause the problem: Insert hidden instructions into a document that enters the approved source, attempting to redirect the AI.
Potential impact: I/mission: Misleading replies, unsafe links or inappropriate task suggestions. C: Disclosure if private information is available in the AI context.
Evidence to check: Source text and provenance, retrieved document version, synthetic attack-test results, generated drafts and review decisions.
Proposed safeguard: Treat documents as reference data. Prevent the drafting AI from executing privileged actions, validate drafts and require staff approval for consequential actions.
How to spot the problem: Flag suspicious passages, unapproved links and replies that conflict with source information. Test indirect injection using synthetic data.
Proposed owner and escalation trigger: AI integration lead. Refer suspicious sources to the content owner; escalate any disclosure or approval bypass immediately to security.
Residual risk: Novel instructions may evade detection, and persuasive incorrect drafts may pass human review.

STRIDE type and service part: Information disclosure: API-to-AI flow, staff workflows, logs and public files
How someone could cause the problem: Paste an identifiable case into an unapproved AI tool, forward excessive context or publish an unredacted debug file.
Potential impact: C/mission: Learner or staff information and credentials are exposed, reducing trust in the service.
Evidence to check: Synthetic outbound-payload tests, provider settings and terms, file-sharing history, repository history and secret-scanning results.
Proposed safeguard: Minimise and redact AI inputs; approve providers; restrict exports; scan public files for secrets; exclude sensitive content from routine logs.
How to spot the problem: Monitor outbound sharing, run secret scans and inspect access settings and redacted test payloads.
Proposed owner and escalation trigger: Service owner and privacy lead. Escalate any exposed secret or real personal data shared outside the approved scope immediately.
Residual risk: Redaction can miss identifying details; provider compromise and previously copied files remain possible.
